subject: Request: Transit key-wrapping traces & ephemeral TLS key provenance
messages:
From: Alice Tan <alice.tan@cloudbank.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: security@cloudbank.com
Date: Thu, 12 Jan 2028 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Request: transit key wrapping traces & TLS ephemeral key provenance

Jonas,

Thanks for taking this — CloudBank's SIG review is in week 3 and we need a short bundle proving the provenance of ephemeral keys used during customer session establishment and the key-wrapping operations for transit. Specifically we want: 
- Per-session TLS ephemeral key indicators (time/window, cipher suite) tied to connection IDs
- Records showing key-wrapping operations (KEK -> DEK wrapping) including HSM operation ids and timestamps
- Evidence of secure deletion for any ephemeral artifacts post-session

Can you confirm what you can provide and the secure transfer mechanism? We can accept an S3 presigned+kms-encrypted bundle or a limited-access SharePoint. Also let us know if any items are redacted by default.

Thanks,
Alice
Alice Tan
CloudBank Security
security@cloudbank.com
From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Alice Tan <alice.tan@cloudbank.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 12 Jan 2028 10:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: transit key wrapping traces & TLS ephemeral key provenance

Alice — appreciate the clear list. We can assemble a compact compliance bundle. High level: 
- Per-session TLS indicators: we can export connection_id -> TLS parameters (timestamp, cipher, ephemeral pubkey hash) for the requested window.
- Key wrapping records: HSM audit IDs, wrap/unlock event timestamps, and wrapping key aliases.
- Secure deletion proof: our runtime records zeroization events and S3 lifecycle markers; we can include a scriptable manifest and SHA256 checksums.

Two quick Qs before we prepare: 
1) Preferred delivery: S3 presigned objects with envelope encryption (byok-wrapped KEK) or an encrypted Box folder? S3 presigned + KMS envelope will be fastest on our side.
2) Scope window: do you want the preceding 7 days, or a specific session date range?

Kimberly and Marissa — looping you in to confirm HSM snapshot availability and any redaction policy for entropy traces.

— Jonas
Jonas Weber
Director, Security Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, Alice Tan <alice.tan@cloudbank.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 12 Jan 2028 14:01:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: transit key wrapping traces & TLS ephemeral key provenance

Hi Alice / team — quick confirmation from the security ops side: 
- We can provide a minimized HSM attestation snapshot (pdf) showing the last successful wrap operations for the KEK aliases used in your tenant binding. That snapshot will include HSM operation ids and attestation cert hashes.
- For TLS ephemeral keys we will include ephemeral public key hashes only (no private material) mapped to connection IDs and timestamps; these are sufficient to show provenance without exposing key material.
- Secure deletion proof: our runtime annotates events with zeroize ops and we will include an S3 lifecycle manifest and the redaction script output (log lines).

We will redact any internal operator account ids; we will not redact HSM operation ids or timestamps. If CloudBank requires operator identifiers for your audit we need an NDA addendum — happy to discuss.

Delivery plan: 
1) We will prepare the bundle for the date range 2028-01-05 -> 2028-01-12 unless you request otherwise.
2) We will upload to a presigned S3 location encrypted with your public KEK; we will share the presigned link and a short checksum manifest.
3) Expected delivery: 2028-01-14 EOD PST.

Attachments (coming with delivery): hsm_attestation_snapshot_20280112.pdf, kms_session_traces_20280114.csv, key_rotation_schedule_q1-2028.csv

Kimberly Park
Sr. Manager, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Appreciate the quick turnaround — can you also include a short mutual action plan (who on your side will own follow-ups)?
